The Concept

One Night, After the
Lights Go Down

For a single October evening, The Old Gallery lifts the velvet ropes, dims its galleries to candlelight, and opens doors that stay closed all year. ARTIFACT: Museum Night is part exhibition, part performance, part secret — a museum reimagined as a stage after dark. Wander freely, follow the gold route, or let the hours carry you from the first footstep to the last echoing note at 2 a.m.

◆

After-Hours Exhibitions

Ninety works from the permanent collection, re-hung for the night under low, warm light — alongside a one-room preview of the autumn acquisitions, shown before the critics see them.

✦

Live Performances

An ambient string quartet in the atrium, a wordless theatre piece among the sculptures, and a closing sound session that lets the building itself hum — all staged inside the galleries.

◈

Guided Hidden-Room Tours

Small groups led through the restoration studio, the print vault and the curator’s corridor — rooms no regular ticket ever opens — with the stories behind what the public never sees.

Program

Eight Hours,
Choreographed in Gold

The night unfolds hour by hour, but nothing is compulsory — every pass moves freely between rooms, and every performance repeats its mood all evening long.

  1. 19:00

    Doors Open

    The gold route lights up across the ground floor. Collect your pass, a floor plan printed on cotton paper, and a first glass of spiced cordial in the foyer.

    Main Entrance
  2. 19:30

    Curator Welcome

    Head curator Dr. Irena Voss opens the night with a ten-minute introduction to the exhibition’s hidden geometry — what to look for, and what was deliberately left in shadow.

    Grand Hall
  3. 20:00

    Hidden Collection Tour

    The first small-group departure into the restoration studio and print vault. White gloves on, voices low — a rare walk through the museum’s working heart.

    Vault Wing
  4. 21:00

    Live Ambient Performance

    The Halicka Quartet performs a slow, circling piece beneath the atrium skylight — strings tuned to the resonance of the marble floor. Seating on velvet benches, standing welcome.

    Atrium
  5. 22:00

    Sculpture Hall Projection

    Light artists Ovid & Marchetti bathe the classical marbles in drifting projections — restoration sketches and lost colours crawling slowly across two thousand years of stone.

    Sculpture Hall
  6. 23:00

    Artist Talk

    A candid, unmoderated conversation with the exhibiting artists — process, failure, and the pieces they almost never finished. Reserved seating for Curator and Patron passes.

    Auditorium
  7. 00:00

    Midnight Gallery Walk

    The lights drop another notch. A silent, self-guided loop through the east wing with only pocket lanterns and the gold route to follow — the quietest hour of the night.

    East Wing
  8. 01:00

    Closing Sound Session

    Sound artist Noor El-Amin sends the night home: a thirty-minute drone composition in the rotunda, built from recordings made inside the building itself.

    Rotunda
"}
